@oomichi thank you for enumerating my concerns, I think I want to explain the reasoning a bit more though:

Master is used interchangeably to refer to different concepts.  Our goal here is not just to use more inclusive language, but to be more specific about what we're referring to.  This includes maintaining the appropriate level of abstraction; sometimes we want to talk about the group as a whole, sometimes we want to talk about a specific instance or member of the group.
- "The thing that hosts all components responsible for controlling my kubernetes cluster" -> **control plane**
- "The thing I talk to in order to interact with my kubernetes cluster" -> **control plane, endpoint**
- "A specific kube-apiserver instance that is part of the kubernetes control plane" -> **apiserver, instance** (this is what I understand `controlplane.Instance` to be)
- "A node that hosts components that are part of the control plane" -> **control plane node**
- "A node that is unschedulable" -> **unschedulable node**
- "A specific component that is part of the control plane" -> **apiserver, controller-manager, scheduler, etcd**

When using terminology that could be seen as generic, ask yourself, is there enough context available to disambiguate potential meanings for the reader? e.g.
- "instance" - an instance of what?
- "apiserver" - is this a generic apiserver? is this a kubernetes apiserver? is this part of the kubernetes control plane?
- "endpoint" - what's at the other end of this endpoint?

I completely agree with @neolit123's comments on capitalization.  I would almost always go with "control plane" in docs or comments.

@oomichi so having said all that, I think your recommendations are solid, except

>Even if node is not added after master, we need to replace the master with control plane node

This is really going to depend on which of the above concepts "master" is referring to.

One other set of assumptions / definition I see come up (in tests, anyway):
- there is exactly one instance of each control plane component
- there is exactly one control plane node that hosts these components

Basically these are assumptions that are tangled up with the e2e framework's concept of a "provider", usually assuming the kube-up.sh gce implementation with a set of default parameters.

We should really be untangling this while we're renaming things, but I don't have a concrete proposal on the best path forward.  Extract operations into the provider interface?  Make a new kind of provider (control plane provider)? Look at cluster provider?

At the very least we should probably ensure names refer to whether they're trying to mutate a single instance of a specific control plane component, all instances, or the control plane in its entirety,
